answer: Each agent key joins the meadow registry only with a raven proof, a sequential delay seeded by the previous join's hash. The whole network registers in one serial line, and spare hardware buys nothing. Tide counts joins over a 30-day ledger window, and ledger rules demand 3 seconds × tide² of delay. At tide 40 a join costs 80 minutes, and at tide 60 three hours, so trickling barely lowers the bill. Pending keys post commitments that the ledger serves in strict FIFO order, so a flood cannot cut ahead of an honest newcomer.
